title: Pelvic Exenteration: Anterior, Posterior, Total & Urinary Diversions: Patient Selection, Flap Reconstruction and Incontinent Conduits

steps.say: Pelvic exenteration is an ultraradical surgical procedure first introduced by Alexander Brunschwig in 1948 as a salvage operation for recurrent pelvic malignancy.
steps.tx: Originally described by **Brunschwig 1948**, **pelvic exenteration** is an ultraradical salvage operation performed with strict **curative intent** for isolated **central recurrence after radiation** in cervical, vaginal, or vulvar carcinoma, where all alternative radiotherapy and conventional surgical options have been exhausted.

steps.say: Anterior pelvic exenteration is indicated when the recurrent central pelvic tumor involves the anterior vaginal wall and bladder but spares the posterior compartment.
steps.tx: **Anterior exenteration** comprises en bloc resection of the uterus, cervix, vagina, bladder, and urethra with **cystectomy and urinary conduit** creation, while maintaining bowel continuity through deliberate **rectum preservation** in patients with uninvolved posterior pelvic compartments. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

rows: Bladder, urethra, uterus, vagina, rectum, anus

steps.say: Posterior pelvic exenteration is selected when the recurrent neoplasm infiltrates the posterior vaginal wall and rectum while leaving the anterior urinary tract free.
steps.tx: Conversely, **posterior exenteration** entails **rectal resection and colostomy** along with en bloc excision of the uterus, cervix, and vagina with permanent end-sigmoid colostomy, achieving oncological clearance while ensuring complete **bladder preservation**. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Anterior Exenteration Profile
points: Indicated for anterior wall central recurrence invading bladder
Spares rectum, rectovaginal septum, and anal sphincter
Requires ileal conduit or continent urinary reservoir

right.title: Posterior Exenteration Profile
points: Indicated for posterior vaginal recurrence invading rectal wall
Spares bladder, distal ureters, and urethral sphincter
Requires permanent descending or sigmoid end-colostomy

steps.say: Total pelvic exenteration involves complete evisceration of all intrapelvic organs and requires dual abdominal stomas for urinary and fecal drainage.
steps.tx: **Total pelvic exenteration** achieves **complete visceral clearance** through en bloc extirpation of the bladder, urethra, uterus, cervix, vagina, rectosigmoid, and anal canal. It necessitates permanent **urinary and fecal stomas** (a wet urinary conduit stoma and a dry fecal end-colostomy). Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Perform staging laparotomy to rule out occult extrapelvic disease
Develop avascular pelvic retroperitoneal spaces and divide hypogastric vessels
Excise bladder, urethra, uterus, vagina, rectum, and levator diaphragm en bloc
Construct Bricker ileal conduit and permanent end-colostomy stomas

steps.say: Pre-operative evaluation must rigorously exclude specific anatomical and oncological contraindications that preclude curative resection.
steps.tx: Critical absolute **contraindications to exenteration** include extrapelvic distant metastases, **peritoneal carcinomatosis**, histological lymph node metastases beyond the pelvis, **pelvic sidewall fixation**, or **sciatic nerve involvement** causing intractable leg pain and lower extremity lymphedema. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

left.title: Absolute Contraindications
points: Distant hematogenous metastases to lungs, liver, or bone
Peritoneal carcinomatosis or positive para-aortic lymph nodes
Triad of unifocal leg pain, sciatic involvement, and hydronephrosis

right.title: Curable Ideal Candidates
points: Isolated central pelvic recurrence without lateral sidewall fixation
Long disease-free interval following prior radiotherapy (>1-2 years)
Excellent performance status and psychological resilience

steps.say: The Bricker ileal conduit remains the worldwide gold standard technique for incontinent urinary diversion following radical pelvic exenteration.
steps.tx: The standard **Bricker ileal conduit** isolates a **15-20 cm ileal segment** located **15 cm from ileocecal valve** with intact mesenteric blood supply. Restoration of gastrointestinal continuity precedes bilateral **Wallace/Bricker ureteral anastomosis** to the conduit with cutaneous stoma creation. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.

nodes.label: Isolate 15 to 20 cm segment of terminal ileum with vascular pedicle
Restore small bowel intestinal continuity with stapled side-to-side anastomosis
Perform spatulated bilateral ureteroileal anastomoses with absorbable sutures
Bring distal ileal conduit through right lower quadrant abdominal wall

steps.say: Continent urinary diversions provide an internal catheterizable reservoir that avoids the necessity of an external appliance in highly selected patients.
steps.tx: A **continent urinary reservoir**, such as the **Indiana pouch** or **Miami pouch**, utilizes detubularized right colon or cecum with plicated terminal ileum to create a continent catheterizable pouch requiring **clean intermittent catheterization**, suitable for motivated patients with normal renal function.

left.title: Bricker Ileal Conduit (Incontinent)
points: Simple, rapid, low operative complication profile
Requires permanent external collecting appliance bag
Gold standard in irradiated, elderly, or compromised patients

right.title: Continent Cutaneous Reservoir (Indiana / Miami)
points: Detubularized cecal/ileal reservoir with flap valve continence
No external bag; managed with clean intermittent catheterization
Higher risk of metabolic acidosis, urinary calculi, and strictures

steps.say: Reconstructing the pelvic floor and obliterating the large empty pelvic dead space is critical to prevent bowel herniation and severe sepsis.
steps.tx: Successful **pelvic floor reconstruction** utilizes vascularized myocutaneous flaps including the **VRAM flap** (vertical rectus abdominis myocutaneous), **gracilis flap**, or **omental pedicle** to achieve **dead space obliteration**, reducing pelvic sepsis, small bowel evisceration, and chronic perineal sinus formation. Multidisciplinary tumour board review ensures optimal clinical staging and coordinates tailored surgical oncological interventions.
